rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aging returns people to the weakness of childhood as God gradually diminishes their abilities, a general human pattern intensified in old age.
rows.anchor: Everyone who passes through childhood and old age experiences this situation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human powers are gifts God may remove, so failing to thank Him and becoming arrogant over them is blameworthy.
rows.anchor: all his abilities and his strengths are bestowed to him by God; He can take them away whenever he wants to

rows.speaker: Most lexicographers
rows.claim: Most lexicographers treat the two verbs for turning back as synonymous.
rows.anchor: Most lexicographers regard سیتنك and نكس to have the same meaning ie. “to make something to turn back.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi argues that the first verb also conveys gradual progression in the reversal, a distinction reflected in both Qur'anic uses.
rows.anchor: in my opinion, the former word also encompasses gradual progression in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here khalq means bodily formation or physical shape.
rows.anchor: The word خلق here means خلقت physical shape) and it is used thus in the Qur’ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah closes by returning to its opening theme: the wise Qur'an validates the Prophet's mission and benefits Arabs, though only spiritually vital people believe.
rows.anchor: the sūrah began with an oath sworn by the Qur’ān replete with wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing passage again validates the Qur'an's claims, beginning by refuting hypocrites who call it poetry and the Prophet a poet.
rows.anchor: Here too, in the concluding section of the sūrah, this sequence can be seen in a new style.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 5–8 describe purposeful creation and cosmic order, establishing God as sole Creator and Lord and human dependence on Him.
rows.anchor: God has created this world with a purpose and there is wisdom behind it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People depend on God, return to Him, and face individual judgment; He knows every deed and hidden secret.
rows.anchor: everyone is destined to return to God; on that Day, no one will bear the burden of any other person

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People call on God in hardship but ignore Him after relief, behaving as if they had never depended on Him.
rows.anchor: when people are afflicted with some hardship, they beseech God and when He delivers them of this hardship they totally ignore Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 9–21 console oppressed monotheists: remain steadfast, migrate if necessary because God's land is spacious, and expect abundant reward.
rows.anchor: If it becomes difficult for them to live in this land, then the land of God is spacious enough for them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet publicly disavows polytheism, while its adherents are warned and those committed to monotheism receive glad tidings.
rows.anchor: a declaration of acquittal is sounded from the tongue of the Prophet (sws) to polytheism and polytheists.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogant deniers of the Qur'an and Prophet are warned; their worldly affluence fuels their arrogance.
rows.anchor: people who are denying the Qur’ān and the Prophet (sws) because of arrogance are warned.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only people with living hearts accept the Qur'an; hardened hearts reject it and face the fate of earlier nations destroyed for rejecting messengers.
rows.anchor: only those people will profess faith in this Qur’ān whose nature is alive

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God assures the Prophet that He alone protects him; no one can withhold God's mercy or avert harm, and the decision belongs to God.
rows.anchor: God is sufficient for his protection; no one can deprive him of God’s mercy if it has been ordained from Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following discussion places life and death entirely under God's authority.
rows.anchor: It is explained that life and death is fully under God’s authority

none: The segment contains the section heading and verse text; its explanation continues in the next segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanzīl means revelation delivered elaborately and thoroughly; the verse reassures the Prophet and warns rejecters.
rows.anchor: it, in fact, means “to reveal in an elaborate manner and with thoroughness.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet neither authored the Book nor asked for it; God revealed it gradually and will establish its truth, while hardship in his mission reflects divine wisdom.
rows.anchor: the Almighty Himself has revealed it to him gradually and is still revealing it to him in this piecemeal manner

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecters must value the Book and accept its guidance; it is God's binding ordinance to obey.
rows.anchor: people should give it due importance and receive the light of guidance from it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing happens without God's directive; all His actions are based on prudence and wisdom.
rows.anchor: nothing happens without His directive and all His actions are based on prudence and wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word haqq means a decisive word, while dīn here means obedience.
rows.anchor: The word  ٌّقT Tَح here means “decisive  word” and the word  ٌنیِد here means “obedience”.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book decisively resolves disputes over monotheism: worship and obey God alone with undivided sincerity because the Creator alone merits both.
rows.anchor: It is totally illogical that the one worshipped should be different to the one shown obedience too.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience to anyone in defiance of God is impermissible, just as worship must be sincere and unadulterated.
rows.anchor: It is not permissible to obey someone in defiance to God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to follow the path determined by revelation; whether others join him is their choice, and he is not responsible for them.
rows.anchor: if others accompany him, it is well and good other he should leave them alone; he is not responsible for them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Associators claim they worship other protectors only as intermediaries to bring them near God; God will judge their dispute on the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: they are only worshipping them because they are a means to procure God’s nearness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb yahdī can mean making someone succeed in an objective; God will not grant success to liars who invent partners or ingrates who credit others for His gifts.
rows.anchor: the Almighty will not make liars and ingrates succeed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both lying about God's partners and thanking others for God's gifts characterize polytheists; they hope their deities will secure divine nearness, but that hope fails.
rows.anchor: Both these attributes are of the polytheists and are necessarily found in every polytheist.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists regard angels as God's daughters and intermediaries; if God wanted children, He would choose the best of His creation.
rows.anchor: they worship the angels after regarding them to be daughters of God and think that they are a means of winning favour with God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted beyond offspring, partners, or helpers; He alone controls the universe.
rows.anchor: He does not need a son or a daughter or any partner or helper.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purposeful creation requires truth and falsehood, virtue and vice to be judged separately; otherwise the world would be meaningless and intercession could falsely guarantee status.
rows.anchor: God has not created the heavens and earth without a purpose. Hence it is not possible that vice and virtue, falsehood and truth not be dealt with separately

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God continuously governs the world: He alternates day and night, serves humanity through the sun and moon, and keeps celestial bodies on fixed schedules.
rows.anchor: it is He alone Who covers the day by the night and covers the night by the day

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is both mighty and forgiving: His might bars unauthorized intercession, while He Himself forgives those worthy of forgiveness.
rows.anchor: Since He is powerful, no one can have access to Him without His permission nor intercede for someone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created every human from one soul and made its mate from the same species; since God alone creates, no other being can be Lord.
rows.anchor: it is God Who has created every one from a single soul, and then created its mate from the same species.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone creates, provides for creatures, and knows all things, so people have no basis for assigning lordship to partners.
rows.anchor: when God is the Creator and He alone has set up this whole system of providence for His creatures

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created livestock as humanity's livelihood and sustenance; the wording 'sent down' like 57:25 points people beyond immediate causes to God, the true source, and fosters gratitude.
rows.anchor: it is God Who sends down all things. He sent down iron and as a result it was produced in the earth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj can mean a pair or one member of it; here it denotes individual male and female animals, eight kinds among four familiar domestic species central to Arab livelihoods.
rows.anchor: Here, it is used in this latter meaning. In Arabia, four types of domestic cattle were very common

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The detailed stages of fetal development in three layers of darkness demonstrate God's creative skill and all-embracing knowledge.
rows.anchor: It is said that it is God Who makes the foetus pass through various phases of creation in the wombs of mothers in three layers darkness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three darknesses are the membrane, womb, and cavity enclosing the womb; God's skill works unseen in darkness, proving His comprehensive knowledge.
rows.anchor: The three layers of darkness refer to the membrane, the womb and the hollow in which the womb is enclosed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive 'where are you turned away?' implies that despite clear evidence people surrender their reins to a devil who leads them from truth.
rows.anchor: they have consigned their reigns to some devil who is leading them into darkness and taking them away from the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here kufr means ingratitude, clarified by its contrast with gratitude; humans need God, whose favor they should acknowledge, while ingratitude displeases Him and brings consequences.
rows.anchor: The word واُرُفْكَت here connotes “ingratitude” and “thanklessness”.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person answers for their own deeds; God knows hearts and presents every person's account, so deities cannot intercede or add to His knowledge.
rows.anchor: each soul is itself answerable to God; no one will be

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People plead humbly to God in calamity, then forget Him after relief, credit divine favors to associates, and mislead others; the verb emphasizes leaders' active misguidance.
rows.anchor: they lead others astray; this is inclusive of the fact that they themselves are already astray.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same pattern recurs at 39:49: human nature knows one God and turns to Him in real need, then forgets Him after relief.
rows.anchor: Human nature is aware of just one God. So whenever a person is in real need, He turns to this God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After relief, people attribute God's favor to other deities or their own ability, thereby making themselves partners to God.
rows.anchor: He then ascribes the favour bestowed to him by God to other supposed deities or to his own capability and intelligence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to warn disbelievers that they have temporary respite to enjoy God's favors but will ultimately face Hell for their misdeeds.
rows.anchor: eventually, they will become the fuel of Hell and it will punish them fully for all their blunders.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse rejects equating the righteous and wrongdoers: people of insight cannot equal those enslaved to desire.
rows.anchor: People having vision and understanding and those who are slaves to their desires cannot be equal in the sight of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oppressed Muslims are urged to persevere in monotheism, assured of abundant reward, and told they may migrate because God's earth is vast.
rows.anchor: if it becomes difficult for them to live in their land, then they should rest assured that vast is God’s earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's forceful disavowal of polytheism shows that coercion and oppression cannot make God's servants submit to it.
rows.anchor: they cannot make God’s servants submit to polytheism through coercion and oppression.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers receive glad tidings; the Prophet's call appeals to people of understanding, and he is not responsible for those whose deeds make them fuel for Hell.
rows.anchor: his call will only appeal to men of understanding; it is not his responsibility to guide those who have become the fuel of Hell

none: This page contains the translated verse text only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic interrogative suppresses an obvious answer; verse 22 uses the same style, leaving the addressee no room to disagree.
rows.anchor: Such a style testifies to the firm conviction of the speaker, and it is also evident from this that there is no room for any difference of opinion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question contrasts the humble night worshipper who fears judgment and hopes for mercy with the arrogant person lacking both; they plainly cannot be equal.
rows.anchor: the two cannot be equal, and this is such an obvious reality that the addressee cannot negate it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession-based salvation wrongly equates the righteous and arrogant, erases concern for God's justice, and makes faith and good deeds seem unnecessary.
rows.anchor: if salvation in the Hereafter depends on the intercession of the deities instead of on faith and righteous deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qunūt means humility before God, best expressed in prayer, especially night prayer, whose privacy rules out pretence and shows true humility.
rows.anchor: The real meaning of ٌوتُنُق is to be humble and modest before God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Standing and prostrating describe prayer postures as well as the worshippers' anxious restlessness while others sleep.
rows.anchor: when others are in deep slumber in their comfortable beds, these people stand and prostrate in prayer before their Lord

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of the Hereafter and hope for God's mercy form the worshippers' inner state and drive their prayer and sacrifice of sleep.
rows.anchor: the fear of the Hereafter and hope of God’s mercy has made them restless

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer's relation with God needs balanced fear and hope: excessive hope breeds indifference and irjāʾ, while excessive fear breeds despair and other evils.
rows.anchor: a person’s relationship with God remains balanced as long as it remains between fear and hope.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic knowledge is knowledge of the universe's origin and end, the Creator's attributes, and humanity's relation to Him; without it even space travel leaves one unguided.
rows.anchor: the real knowledge needed to be guided in life is that a person knows the origin of this universe and its end
